<reason>CON won the marginal-deal comparison. PRO showed some mergers harm prices/innovation but never proved the additional deals caught by stricter 4-to-3/vertical presumptions are net harmful. CON answered pass-through pressure honestly, distinguished killer vs capability deals, and exposed PRO's weighing error: motion counts lost productivity/scale even without immediate discounts, and blocking harm can be permanent loss of financing/development, not temporary paperwork. PRO's closing misread nothing-guarantees as concession.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's weighing correction that only-passed-through efficiencies count shifts the goalposts and that irreversibility cuts both ways — a missed window can mean no product — which directly neutralized PRO's temporary-friction vs permanent-harm asymmetry.</best_rebuttal>
